content.comment_body: Hello, I use Windows XP, Windows 8, and MacOS for different purposes, mainly using my Mac since it suits me best. I'm facing problems connecting my Mac OS X 10.9.1 with my [product_name] device using the USB adapter provided by [company_name]. The cable functions on the XP computer. I'm using [product_name] software version [version_no], which works on the Mac but has some bugs. However, when attempting transfers, the COM port option isn't visible. I downloaded the driver from [company_name], but Mac reports it as corrupt and suggests removing it. I copied the USB driver into the [product_name] directory and ran it there, but it still didn't work. The driver from the supplied disk also fails. This is quite frustrating. Any advice would be appreciated!

Hi, [product_name] version [version_no] is officially compatible with Mac OS X 10.5 running J2SE 1.6.0. You might try installing the USB cable driver manually. The driver on the [product_name] DVD likely won't work, so check Silicon Labs' website for a suitable Mac OS X driver. Also, take a look at the Readme file in the USB driver folder on the DVD. If none of these options succeed, you may need to wait until your OS X version is formally supported by [product_name]. Hope this helps.
Thank you [user_name] for your help. If I find a solution, I'll share a guide here.

As promised, I'm updating after successfully resolving the issue. After gathering information, I found a solution that works. Using OS X Mavericks 10.9.1 and the latest [product_name] version [version_no], I discovered the best way to update [product_name] is through its built-in update feature, not via [company_name]'s website. After following the recommended steps, I've managed to transfer programs between the [product_name] hardware and my MacBook Pro. Here’s what I did: 1. Update [product_name] using the instructions above. 2. In Finder, use 'Go' and 'Go to Folder' to open '/var'. 3. Create a 'lock' folder there, if it doesn't exist. 4. Ensure the 'lock' folder and '/var' directory are readable and writable by everyone (use 'Get Info' and adjust permissions). 5. Also check 'var/spool/uucp' permissions. 6. Download the USB to UART CP2102 driver from Silabs—drivers from [company_name]'s website did not work. 7. Install the Silabs driver. If blocked due to unknown developer, right-click and select 'Open' while holding ctrl to bypass security. 8. Once installed, restart your computer. 9. After reboot, use Disk Utility to repair permissions on your main drive. 10. Connect the USB cable to [product_name] device, making sure it's powered on. 11. Open [product_name] and configure the USB COM port under Tools > Options > Interface; select among the available ports. 12. You can now transfer as usual. This should help—it worked for me after considerable effort. [company_name] should improve this process, as I had no success on Windows 8 and my old XP laptop is failing. Regards.

analysis.insight_summary: Users attempting to run [product_name] software on newer MacOS versions encountered persistent issues with USB driver compatibility and software stability. The officially supplied drivers from [company_name] were often flagged as corrupt or incompatible, leaving users to manually adjust system folder permissions and rely on third-party drivers to resolve USB communication problems. Documentation for these steps is lacking, causing notable frustration during installation and use.
analysis.user_expectations: Users desire straightforward installation and reliable operation of [product_name] software on MacOS, including bundled drivers that work seamlessly and easy connection between software and hardware. They expect official support for current MacOS versions and better documentation for troubleshooting USB compatibility issues.
